questions.question: Contract costing is NOT used in one of the following industries.
A contract is generally of ________ duration.
Retention money serves as a ________ with the contractee.
If retention money is 13% of work certified, the cash ratio is ________.
Sub-contract cost is always treated as a ________ to the contract.
When the completion stage of a contract is more than half but not substantially complete, the profit to be credited to the Profit and Loss Account is generally ________.
options: A. 2/3 of notional profit × cash received ÷ work certified
B. 1/2 of notional profit × cash received ÷ work certified
C. 1/3 of notional profit × cash received ÷ work certified

questions.question: Departments are usually located in the ________.
Departmental accounting facilitates ________.
Indirect expenses are also called ________.
Expenses which can be apportioned to departments are shown in the ________.
options: D. Profit and loss appropriation account

questions.question: When goods are transferred from one department to another department, it is called ________.
When goods are transferred from one department to another, the department transferring the goods should be ________.
When goods are transferred from one department to another, the transferring department is credited while the receiving department is ________.
In departmental accounts, expenses such as directors' fees and interest are transferred to the ________.
options: C. Profit and loss appropriation account
D. General profit and loss account

questions.question: Departmental accounting enables a business firm to maximize ________.
A branch which does not maintain its own complete set of books is called a ________.
A branch whose business policies and administration are wholly controlled by the head office is a ________.
Branches which do not keep a full system of accounting are called ________.
A dependent branch may make ________.
Under the Branch Account Debtors System, closing balances of branch assets are recorded on the ________ of the Branch Account.
Under the Branch Debtors System, bad debts and discounts allowed to debtors are ________ in the Branch Account.
options: A. Shown on the debit side
B. Shown on the credit side
C. Shown on the asset side

questions.question: Under the Branch Debtors System, the Branch Account is used to determine the ________.
The difference between goods sent by the head office and goods received by the branch is known as ________.
The hire purchase system in Nigeria is principally governed by the ________.
The system of acquiring an asset by paying an initial deposit and the balance by installments, while ownership passes after the final payment, is known as ________.
What is transferred to the hirer immediately under a hire purchase system?
options: B. Ownership and possession of the asset

questions.question: The price at which goods can be purchased outright by the hirer for ready cash is known as the ________.
A contract offer that is written on paper, signed, sealed and delivered is known as a ________.
An offer of a contract can be terminated by: I. Revocation II. Lapse of offer III. Consignment.
Expenses applicable specifically to a particular contract are debited to the ________.
Departments A and B have sales of ₦5,000 and ₦6,000 respectively. If total selling expenses of ₦660 are apportioned on turnover basis, what is the selling expense allocated to Department A?
Departments A and B have sales of ₦5,000 and ₦6,000 respectively. If total selling expenses of ₦660 are apportioned on turnover basis, what is the selling expense allocated to Department B?
Departments A and B have total sales of ₦11,000 and total selling expenses of ₦660. What is their combined net result after deducting the selling expenses?
Which of the following is the appropriate basis for apportioning rent among departments?
A branch is a unit of a business organization which is not located on the same premises as the head office.
In branch accounting, another name for invoice price is ________.
A branch whose accounting records are wholly or mainly maintained by the head office is called a ________.
Goods supplied to a dependent branch by the head office may be sent at: I. Invoice price II. Cost price III. Cost plus mark-up.
When the head office maintains all the books of account, goods sent to a branch are credited to the ________.
options: D. Goods sent to branch account

questions.question: The initial sum payable by the hire purchase buyer at the beginning of the hire purchase transaction is called the ________.
In a hire purchase transaction, the asset acquired by the hirer is usually classified as a ________.
Under a hire purchase agreement, ownership of the property remains with the hirer before the final installment is paid.
The taking back of goods from a customer who fails to keep up with hire purchase payments is called ________.
Where goods are invoiced by a firm to its branch at cost plus a mark-up, the Branch Stock Adjustment Account is used to determine ________.
Where the head office maintains all books of account, goods sent to a branch are credited to the ________.
options: A. Goods sent to branch account

questions.question: Goods sent to a branch may be recorded in the head office books at: I. Selling price II. Cost price plus mark-up III. Cost price.
Rent owed by a department at the end of an accounting period is treated in the balance sheet as a ________.
In departmental accounts, administration expenses are recorded in the ________.
options: D. Profit and loss appropriation account

questions.question: The cost of carriage outward is classified as a ________.
The assumption that a business will continue to operate into the foreseeable future is emphasized by the ________ concept.
